sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *haber de* + infinitive from B2 Unit 26, the formal pattern for a duty (*He de reconocer ...*) and for "was to" in a story (*había de cambiar ...*). Texts about laws and about history use it. Here it works on indigenous lands and the Xingu park.

sections.title: haber de + infinitive
rows: El Estado ha de proteger las tierras indígenas.
a duty: the State must protect
Los visitantes han de pedir permiso para entrar en una tierra indígena.
Los hermanos Villas-Bôas habían de crear el Parque del Xingu en 1961.
in a story: they were to create
Aquella decisión había de cambiar la política hacia los pueblos indígenas.
in a story: it was to change

items.spanish: La Funai ha de vigilar los territorios de los pueblos aislados.
items.english: Funai must watch over the territories of isolated peoples.

items.spanish: Los poderes públicos han de respetar la Constitución de 1988.
items.english: Public authorities must respect the Constitution of 1988.

items.spanish: El parque había de ser un refugio para varios pueblos.
items.english: The park was to be a refuge for several peoples.

sections.content: *Haber de* changes with the person (*he de*, *ha de*, *han de*, *habían de*), but *hay que* never does. It is formal: in everyday speech people say *tiene que* or *debe*. Do not leave out *de*.
